rules.title: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6
rules.requirement: A landlord or their agent may charge an application screening fee to an applicant to cover costs of obtaining information about the applicant, but the fee shall not exceed the actual out-of-pocket costs and reasonable time spent, and in no case be greater than $30 per applicant, adjusted annually by CPI starting January 1, 1998. The fee may only be charged if a rental unit is available and the landlord offers a compliant screening process.
rules.summary_plain: Landlords in California can charge up to $30 (adjusted yearly for inflation) to cover screening costs when you apply to rent, but only if a unit is available and they follow fair screening rules.
rules.summary_plain_es: Los propietarios en California pueden cobrar hasta $30 (ajustados anualmente por inflación) para cubrir los costos de evaluación cuando solicitas alquilar, pero solo si hay una unidad disponible y siguen reglas justas de evaluación.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to all residential rental property rental applications in California.
rules.exemptions_text: No application screening fee may be charged if no rental unit is available or will be available within a reasonable time.
rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding Section 1950.5, when a landlord or their agent receives a request to rent a residential property from an applicant, the landlord or their agent may charge, pursuant to subdivision (c), that applicant an application screening fee to cover the costs of obtaining information about the applicant. ... (b) The amount of the application screening fee shall not be greater than the actual out-of-pocket costs ... In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
